notes.title: Release Window + New Trailer Premiere @ Top Hat Studios Showcase
notes.notes:
Hello everyone!

We're happy to announce that as part of the Top Hat Studios Publisher Showcase, we've debuted a brand new trailer! 

[previewyoutube=G0MBQHQh62c;full][/previewyoutube]

As part of the this debut, we're also happy to announce that we finally have a release window for Windswept - Summer 2025! Stay tuned as we reveal more specific information soon. Thank you for your support!

notes.title: Important update about Windswept...
notes.notes:
Hi there!
Sorry for the clickbait it's just a normal update (but every update is important, so...)

I know many of you out there have been eager to receive information from me so allow me to break the silence by using a recent quote from another Australian dev team:

"Windswept is real, progressing, and will release."

*mic drop*

There you have it folks, worry not!

But seriously, I'm sorry I haven't been as active with these news updates. It's hard being Mr WeatherFell in every facet of the development process and I've been super busy just making the game and trying to garner more attention for it on socials.

The FACTS!
Windswept is "done"
Yep! Every stage in Windswept has been made, the beginning of the end starts now.
I was given instructions back in July that I should get all of Windswept's content made by the end of January in order to ensure the game has a smooth porting/localization process (that's next week OH NO).

Content in this context means I need every stage, menu, overworld, minigame, etc. functional and playable from start to end.

Anyway, since July I've been on a 6-month crunch to get everything done in time, I've had to take holiday hours off work, cut back on all my hobbies and put some other life events on hold in order to get to where we are right now. I'm not saying any of this to garner pity or sympathy, it's just how it turned out and I did what I deemed necessary to ensure things stay on track. In addition to this, I've had to fulfill my Kickstarter responsibility of releasing World 3's beta in September and World 4's beta in December to eligible backers, that latter update was so riddled with bugs due to this content crunch I simply didn't announce it here just until I could find the time to fix them all up first

So yeah, that's why my updates haven't been as timely as they used to be, I've been grinding!

You: Show me the stuff!
Me: Soon! Eventually! Promise!
Gathering screenshots and video footage is another time sink I unfortunately don't have the capacity to manage right now, sorry!
The best I can do for now is drop some of the "is this marketing? 👋🦋" footage I've been posting on Twitter and Bluesky.

It's truly all I can manage for now, I just wanted to touch base and keep you all in the loop! Next update will possibly be a release date announcement. Or maybe it won't. But it could be... Unless it isn't!

And if Silksong drops in our release window so help me!

notes.title: Dev Log #6 - Slow-vember Update
notes.notes:
Howdy gamers and welcome to the Kickstarter November Update!

If you don't follow me on Twitter (you should), I mentioned November is my birth month. I've spent most of the time taking my foot off the pedal to chill for a bit (feel free to comment happy birthday - it was a week ago though so it's whatever!)

You know where I'm going with this - it's time for a relatively short update for a slow-ish month!

Most of the time was spent cleaning up existing systems, it's hard to make that sound interesting but let's give it a go...

Screen Transitions
Transitions add so much to a game when used effectively - Windswept had a couple but they were very rigid in their execution, so I needed a better solution.

https://ksr-ugc.imgix.net/assets/043/115/534/c2021af4eec051b7f6512e154e0e48aa_original.gif?ixlib=rb-4.1.0&w=700&fit=max&v=1700386488&gif-q=50&q=92&s=fb452f670859bc4963c20a9a6a983453

The old transition system was sort of like the gif above, where the fade-in to fade-out were a fixed duration and the game just sorta waited for it to finish before continuing. The new system lets me determine the duration and specifics of every step in the process. If I want the screen to stay black until another system tells it to proceed, I can now!

https://ksr-ugc.imgix.net/assets/043/115/532/f04b0c0a80b8301c2a06bf246131f680_original.gif?ixlib=rb-4.1.0&w=700&fit=max&v=1700386469&gif-q=50&q=92&s=420a58956e44dd38ee8795b17dbd7f5e

Additionally, I can specify different graphics to cut out of the blackness. I can also lock-on to a specific target to draw more focus to it. This will come in handy for Laamp's coin search service and any other situation I need to move your eyes to another part of the screen more naturally.

The Scoreboard

https://ksr-ugc.imgix.net/assets/043/115/562/366c8b34795b7cd6e1b8cbd55b970499_original.png?ixlib=rb-4.1.0&w=700&fit=max&v=1700386978&gif-q=50&lossless=true&s=f7bb526cd292ed648979c52e606d1f82

Support for achievements is baked right into the game for situations where the platform hosting Windswept doesn't support them natively. The goal will be to have pixel art icons that can be reused for Steam's achievement icons. I'm particularly fond of the memorable icons used in Yoshi's Island to give players a clear understanding of what each stage is without having to play it. Be sure to give Woodspixl_ all of your energy, this job rests with her!

Music and Sound
Lemme be real for a sec, professional music and sound is expensive and that part of development was one of the main contributors to why I came to Kickstarter in the first place. With Windswept being my first commercial project, I was faced with a lot of tricky decisions while using my own personal finances in the early days.

95% of the music & sound in our demo was made to help tie the project together in preparation for the KS campaign. The campaign's level of success would go on to determine the number of sounds produced and the amount of times music would repeat throughout the game.

All that to say FatBard have added their first contributions to the game in over a year! Here's a brief showcase of some things they've done since returning.

[previewyoutube=O-W2rFia9N4;full][/previewyoutube]

There's still a bit of balancing to do and whatnot but overall it's breathing new life into the project at a time when I really need it to. Motivation is at an all-time high until the bill arrives!

As the year's coming to a close I'm trying to cram in everything I need to before entering the final phase of development - the content!

I think next month's update is gonna be quite big, so long as I'm able to deliver on what I set out to do! Guess we'll have to wait until then, byeeeeeee!
